added_lemmas.statement:
Theorem 1 (pairwise positive-chamber decision).  For every finite input \(\mathfrak u\) accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\), every \(D,D'\in\mathfrak D\), and every outcome cell \(y\), define, for each bit-zero conditional-independence statement \(c\),
\[
 h_c(p)=\sum_{g\in\mathcal C_0(\mathcal I,c)}g(p)^2.
\]
There is a terminating exact real-closed-field decision procedure for the sentence
\[
 \exists p\in\mathbb R^\Omega\left[
 \sum_{z\in\Omega}p_z=1
 \ \wedge\ 
 \bigwedge_{g\in\mathcal C_1(\mathcal I)}g(p)=0
 \ \wedge\ 
 \bigwedge_{z\in\Omega}p_z>0
 \ \wedge\ 
 \bigwedge_{c:\mathcal I(c)=0}h_c(p)>0
 \ \wedge\ 
 F_{D,D',y}(p)\neq0
 \right].
\]
Exactly one of the following certificates is returned.  If the sentence is feasible, the procedure returns an exact real-algebraic table \(p^\dagger\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\cap\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}^\Omega\), encoded by a rational univariate representation together with coordinate minimal polynomials and rational isolating or Thom data, such that
\[
 T_{D,y}(p^\dagger)\neq T_{D',y}(p^\dagger).
\]
If the sentence is infeasible, it returns a finite quantifier-elimination trace or Positivstellensatz identity proving
\[
 T_{D,y}(p)=T_{D',y}(p)
 \qquad\text{for every }p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}.
\]
Thus feasibility is the complete pairwise separation criterion on the positive exact-oracle chamber, and infeasibility is the complete universal-equality criterion on that chamber.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix an input \(\mathfrak u\) accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\), graphs \(D,D'\in\mathfrak D\), and an outcome cell \(y\).  For every conditional-independence statement \(c\) with \(\mathcal I(c)=0\), put
\[
 h_c(p)=\sum_{g\in\mathcal C_0(\mathcal I,c)}g(p)^2.
\tag{1}
\]
Define finite subsets of \(\mathbb Q[p_z:z\in\Omega]\) by
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E&=\mathcal C_1(\mathcal I)\cup
 \left\{\sum_{z\in\Omega}p_z-1\right\},\\
 G&=\{p_z:z\in\Omega\}\cup
 \{h_c:\mathcal I(c)=0\},\\
 H&=\{p_z:z\in\Omega\}\cup
 \{h_c:\mathcal I(c)=0\}\cup\{F_{D,D',y}\}.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
These sets are finite because \(V\), each \(\Omega_v\), and the collection of conditional-independence statements on \(V\) are finite by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\).  They have rational coefficients: the minors in \(\mathcal C_1(\mathcal I)\) and \(\mathcal C_0(\mathcal I,c)\) have integer coefficients by their determinantal definitions, the normalization polynomial has integer coefficients, (1) is a finite sum of squares, and \(F_{D,D',y}\) is an integer polynomial by \(\mathrm{def{:}pairwise\text{-}cross\text{-}signature}\).

Use the notation \(S(E,G,H)\) of \(\mathrm{lem{:}semialgebraic\text{-}decision\text{-}with\text{-}certificates}\).  For every cell \(z\), the two conditions \(p_z\geq0\) from \(G\) and \(p_z\neq0\) from \(H\) are equivalent over \(\mathbb R\) to \(p_z>0\).  For every bit-zero statement \(c\), equation (1) implies \(h_c(p)\geq0\) for every real table \(p\), so the conditions \(h_c(p)\geq0\) and \(h_c(p)\neq0\) are equivalent to \(h_c(p)>0\).  The equalities indexed by \(E\) are exactly normalization and all bit-one oracle equalities, while the remaining inequation in \(H\) is \(F_{D,D',y}(p)\neq0\).  Therefore \(\mathrm{def{:}exact\text{-}oracle\text{-}model}\) gives the set identity
\[
 S(E,G,H)
 =\left\{p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}:
 F_{D,D',y}(p)\neq0\right\}.
\tag{3}
\]

Apply \(\mathrm{lem{:}semialgebraic\text{-}decision\text{-}with\text{-}certificates}\) to the sets in (2), with \(k=|\Omega|\).  Its exact algorithm terminates and decides whether the set in (3) is empty.  The nonempty and empty cases are mutually exclusive and exhaustive.

Suppose first that the set in (3) is nonempty.  The decision lemma returns an exactly encoded point
\[
 p^\dagger\in S(E,G,H)\cap\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}^\Omega,
\tag{4}
\]
represented by a rational univariate representation together with coordinate minimal polynomials and rational isolating or Thom data.  Combining (3) and (4) yields
\[
 p^\dagger\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}
 \cap\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}^\Omega,
 \qquad
 F_{D,D',y}(p^\dagger)\neq0.
\tag{5}
\]
Every observed-table marginal occurring as a denominator factor in the truncated factorization is a sum over a nonempty collection of cells.  Strict positivity in \(\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\), used in (5), makes each such marginal strictly positive.  By the denominator-recording rule in \(\mathrm{def{:}truncated\text{-}functional}\), the reduced denominators are products of the uncancelled positive marginal factors; hence
\[
 B_{D,y}(p^\dagger)>0,
 \qquad
 B_{D',y}(p^\dagger)>0.
\tag{6}
\]
The identity in \(\mathrm{def{:}pairwise\text{-}cross\text{-}signature}\), with division justified by (6), now gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 T_{D,y}(p^\dagger)-T_{D',y}(p^\dagger)
 &=\frac{A_{D,y}(p^\dagger)}{B_{D,y}(p^\dagger)}
   -\frac{A_{D',y}(p^\dagger)}{B_{D',y}(p^\dagger)}\\
 &=\frac{A_{D,y}(p^\dagger)B_{D',y}(p^\dagger)
          -A_{D',y}(p^\dagger)B_{D,y}(p^\dagger)}
         {B_{D,y}(p^\dagger)B_{D',y}(p^\dagger)}\\
 &=\frac{F_{D,D',y}(p^\dagger)}
         {B_{D,y}(p^\dagger)B_{D',y}(p^\dagger)}\neq0.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{7}
\]
Thus the feasible branch returns the required exact real-algebraic positive-chamber separator, and its encoding is checkable by the exact algebraic-number arithmetic guaranteed by the decision lemma.

Suppose instead that the set in (3) is empty.  The same decision lemma returns a finite identity
\[
 a_0+b_0+c_0^2=0,
 \qquad
 a_0\in\langle E\rangle,
 \quad b_0\in\operatorname{PO}(G),
 \quad c_0\in\operatorname{Mon}(H),
\tag{8}
\]
over a finite real algebraic extension of \(\mathbb Q\); equivalently, a finite quantifier-elimination trace may certify the same infeasibility conclusion.  By (3), exact infeasibility implies
\[
 F_{D,D',y}(p)=0
 \qquad\text{for every }p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}.
\tag{9}
\]
Fix any \(p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\).  The positivity argument establishing (6), now applied to \(p\), gives
\[
 B_{D,y}(p)B_{D',y}(p)>0.
\tag{10}
\]
Equations (9)--(10) and the pairwise cross-signature identity imply
\[
 T_{D,y}(p)-T_{D',y}(p)
 =\frac{F_{D,D',y}(p)}{B_{D,y}(p)B_{D',y}(p)}=0.
\tag{11}
\]
Since \(p\) was arbitrary, the two functionals are universally equal on \(\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\).

Conversely, if the functionals differ at some \(p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\), denominator positivity as in (10) and the pairwise identity force \(F_{D,D',y}(p)\neq0\), so (3) is nonempty.  Hence feasibility is exactly pairwise separation on the declared positive exact-oracle chamber, whereas infeasibility is exactly universal equality there.  No conclusion is drawn from real-radical nonmembership alone.
added_lemmas.justification: This is the load-bearing pairwise positive-chamber decision: it distinguishes universal equality from a pair-indexed causal separator using exact, independently checkable semialgebraic certificates.
added_lemmas.gap: Garcia, Stillman, and Sturmfels do not select the strictly positive exact-oracle chamber, and Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo provide no general construction of separators on that chamber.
added_lemmas.consumer: SparseSIM-ID can compare arbitrary tied graphs directly and return either a certified within-class equality or an exact real-algebraic ambiguity table.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The replacement theorem is strictly stronger, treats arbitrary \(D,D'\in\mathfrak D\), and removes the obsolete reference-graph and rational-separation framing. Deletion with a replacement preserves inbound dependency migration without misclassifying the strengthening as a narrowing.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: The graph-indexed family \(\{P_x^D(Y=y):D\in\mathfrak D\}\), its unique maximal equality quotient on \(\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\), and the class-specific vectors \(\tau_C(P)\) for fixed returned quotient classes \(C\).
proposed_core_edits.reason: The estimand line must expose both the maximal pairwise quotient and the class-specific causal vectors covered by fixed-class inference.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: For each returned class \(C\) with canonical representative \(R_C\), define \(\tau_C(p)=(T_{R_C,y}(p))_y\). Under a compatible Markovian structural causal model, \(P_x^D(Y=y)=T_{D,y}(p)=T_{R_C,y}(p)=\tau_{C,y}(p)\) for every \(D\in C\), every outcome cell \(y\), and every \(p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\). Conditional on a fixed or externally certified true class \(C\), the plug-in procedure estimates \(\tau_C(P)\); no claim is made for inference after data-driven class or oracle selection. When the quotient has one class, \(\tau_C\) is the common law \(P_x(Y)\) across all tied graphs.
proposed_core_edits.reason: The previous line advertised only the common one-class circuit and did not state the class-indexed target or the fixed-class scope of inference.

proposed.comparator_claim: Theorem 3.2 gives a sufficient graphical condition for simultaneous identification over a finite SA-MPDAG family.

Theorem 3.6 gives a necessary-and-sufficient criterion and generalized truncated factorization for one MPDAG; the present proof uses only the graph-specific functional substrate and makes no extensional-equivalence claim.
Theorem 8 identifies a DAG factorization component by saturation of local and global Markov ideals.

Theorem 3 minimally enumerates distinct intervention functionals represented by one MPDAG; any class it certifies as one graph-generic functional is contained in a SparseSIM-ID class when the exact-oracle model lies in that MPDAG Markov model, with no converse claimed.
IDP is sound and complete for causal-effect identification from one PAG.
A discrete causal query under one specified model compiles to a sharp polynomial program with anytime-valid outer bounds.

Resampling conditional-independence statistics and unioning graphwise intervals yields asymptotically correct coverage after PC discovery; the present result instead gives pointwise Wald inference for a fixed or externally certified quotient class and makes no post-selection claim.
SP consistently recovers the true MEC under the sparsest Markov representation condition; the present algorithm instead retains every minimum-edge I-map tie before quotienting by the causal query.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The comparison record must distinguish fixed-class Wald inference from Chang--Guo--Malinsky post-selection coverage while preserving the existing graphical comparator scopes.

prose_updates.tldr: SparseSIM-ID starts from finite state spaces, an exact conditional-independence oracle, background orientations, and a causal query; a rational realization and a compressed graph family are optional checked accelerators. It certifies oracle realizability, exhaustively constructs every minimum-edge DAG I-map, and uses exact pairwise positive-chamber decisions to compute the unique coarsest quotient whose classes share \(P_x(Y)\) on the strictly positive exact-oracle model. Each pairwise decision returns either a finite universal-equality certificate or an exact real-algebraic positive ambiguity table. Normalization reduces the all-pairs feasibility count to \(\binom{|\mathfrak D|}{2}(\prod_{v\in Y}|\Omega_v|-1)\), and the reference-only common-effect test to \((|\mathfrak D|-1)(\prod_{v\in Y}|\Omega_v|-1)\). For every fixed or externally certified true quotient class \(C\), the representative circuit supports a multivariate plug-in central limit theorem, consistent sandwich covariance, and Wald intervals for fixed contrasts; this is not inference after data-driven oracle or class selection. The explicit four-binary-variable rational cross-MEC witness remains a strictness certificate.

project_justification.gap: Existing simultaneous-identification criteria are sufficient graphical tests and do not compute the maximal law-restricted effect quotient across all tied minimum-edge DAG I-maps. Saturated conditional-independence ideals also do not select strict positivity or the bit-zero exact-oracle chamber, and a one-class inferential formulation omits valid class-specific targets when several effect classes are returned.
project_justification.niche: For finite observed variables, the exact oracle, every admissible DAG, every graphwise truncated functional, and every arbitrary-pair positive-chamber equality test are finite and exact. This makes the tied-sparsest family and its maximal causal-effect quotient computable, while a fixed representative circuit in any returned class is an ordinary smooth rational functional at a strictly positive law.
project_justification.fill: The project gives a terminating realizability-first algorithm that enumerates all minimum-edge I-map ties, partitions them through exact pairwise semialgebraic decisions, and certifies every merge or separation. It returns one observable circuit per class and algebraic-number ambiguity witnesses across classes. Conditional on fixing or externally certifying the true quotient class, it also supplies class-specific plug-in Gaussian inference, a consistent sandwich covariance, and Wald intervals for arbitrary fixed nondegenerate contrasts.

sampling_model.design: Independent sampling from one fixed strictly positive multinomial law \(P\), conditional on a real-realizable exact oracle, its tied minimum-edge family, and one true returned quotient class \(C\) having been fixed in advance or certified externally; the class is not selected from the same sample used for inference.
sampling_model.overlap: Membership \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\) gives positive cells and therefore positive recorded marginal denominators for every representative circuit at the fixed law.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no nonparametric nuisances. For the canonical representative \(R_C\), compute \(\widehat\tau_{C,n}=\tau_C(\widehat p_n)\), \(\widehat\Sigma_n=\operatorname{diag}(\widehat p_n)-\widehat p_n\widehat p_n^{\mathsf T}\), and \(\widehat V_{C,n}=J_{\tau_C}(\widehat p_n)\widehat\Sigma_nJ_{\tau_C}(\widehat p_n)^{\mathsf T}\) on the positive-denominator event.

prose_updates.related_work: Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo (2025, Theorem 3.2 and Section 4.2) give the closest simultaneous-identification boundary: their SA-MPDAG condition is sufficient, whereas SparseSIM-ID decides and certifies the complete effect quotient of every finite tied minimum-edge I-map family. The preserved four-node rational example lies outside that graphical sufficient region and has two distinct causal values. Perkovic (2020, Theorem 3.6) supplies single-MPDAG identification structure, but no extensional equivalence with the present law-restricted cross-family quotient is claimed. Guo and Perkovic (2021, Theorem 3) minimally enumerate graph-generic effect functionals within one MPDAG; the proved relation is one-way: a class they certify as one functional is contained in a SparseSIM-ID class whenever the exact-oracle model is contained in that MPDAG's positive Markov model. Garcia, Stillman, and Sturmfels (2005) inform saturation, while Tarski's decision method and Stengle's Positivstellensatz provide supporting exact feasibility machinery rather than the causal novelty. Kahle, Rauh, and Sullivant (2017) explain why irrelevant conditional-independence components preclude reading positive exact-oracle separation from ideal nonmembership. Raskutti and Uhler (2018) motivate retention of all sparsest ties; the new output policy quotients those ties by the causal query. Chang, Guo, and Malinsky (2024) provide post-PC selection-aware interval unions, whereas the present plug-in theorem is pointwise for a fixed or externally certified true quotient class and explicitly makes no claim after data-driven class or oracle selection. Jaber, Zhang, and Bareinboim (2019) and Duarte et al. (2024) remain adjacent completeness and optimization comparators rather than equivalent results.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Termination and the numbers of pairwise positive-chamber comparisons are explicit, but no favorable running-time, degree, certificate-length, or algebraic-height bound is claimed. The default DAG enumeration is finite and may be exponential or worse. Saturation by cells and denominators excludes components contained in their zero sets but imposes neither positivity nor bit-zero nonvanishing, so a nonzero normal form is only a feasibility trigger. General feasible separators are guaranteed to be exact real algebraic, not rational. The rational-replacement question remains open only for an already feasible set \(\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\cap\{F_{D,D',y}\neq0\}\) and is not needed for pairwise decision or quotient completeness. The plug-in central limit theorem is conditional on a fixed or externally certified true quotient class; uniformity and post-selection coverage after estimating the oracle or class are not established.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The required inputs are finite state spaces, a complete exact conditional-independence bit-vector, background orientations, and a causal query. A rational realization and a compressed SA-MPDAG or CPDAG family are optional checked accelerators, not assumptions. Unrealizable exact oracles and background systems admitting no I-map receive finite rejection certificates; every real-realizable oracle with at least one admissible DAG proceeds to the complete tied minimum-edge quotient. Each arbitrary-pair decision returns either exact universal-equality evidence or an exact real-algebraic positive separator. Separators need not be rational, and no polynomial-time or uniform height guarantee is made. The quotient is law-restricted and can be coarser than a graph-generic within-MPDAG enumeration; only the proved one-way Guo--Perkovic containment is claimed. The four-variable table remains an explicit rational cross-MEC separator with values \(13/20\) and \(1/2\). Plug-in inference applies to every fixed or externally certified true quotient class and to fixed nondegenerate contrasts, but it is pointwise and is not selection-aware inference for an oracle, graph family, or class estimated from the same data.

statement_notes.justification: This theorem is the exact pairwise kernel of the maximal quotient: for any two tied DAGs and any outcome cell, it produces independently checkable evidence for either universal equality or positive-chamber separation.
statement_notes.gap: Ideal nonmembership can be witnessed on an irrelevant component or sign chamber, so neither saturation nor a nonzero normal form decides separation on the strictly positive exact-oracle model.
statement_notes.consumer: The quotient algorithm can merge arbitrary graph pairs only with equality certificates and split them only with an exact real-algebraic table at which their intervention laws differ.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(\mathfrak u\), \(C\), \(R_C\), and \(P\) as in the theorem.  Membership of \(C\) in the quotient returned by \(\mathrm{thm{:}sparse\text{-}simid\text{-}completeness}\) gives, for every \(D\in C\), every outcome cell \(y\), and every \(p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\),
\[
 T_{D,y}(p)=T_{R_C,y}(p). \tag{61}
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem{:}common\text{-}law\text{-}redundancy}\), \(P\) is Markov to every \(D\in\mathfrak D\), in particular to each \(D\in C\).  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}dag\text{-}intervention\text{-}functional}\), every recursive Markovian structural causal model compatible with such a \(D\) and having observational law \(P\) satisfies
\[
 P_x^D(Y=y)=T_{D,y}(P). \tag{62}
\]
Taking \(p=P\) in (61) and combining (61) with (62) yields, coordinate by coordinate,
\[
 P_x^D(Y=y)=T_{D,y}(P)=T_{R_C,y}(P)=\tau_{C,y}(P),
 \qquad D\in C. \tag{63}
\]
Thus \(\tau_C(P)=P_x^D(Y)\) is derived from the graph-specific truncated factorization and the returned equality quotient; it is not defined to be the causal law.

By \(\mathrm{lem{:}truncated\text{-}vector\text{-}normalization}\), strict positivity of \(P\), as encoded by \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\), implies
\[
 B_{R_C,y}(P)>0 \qquad\text{for every outcome cell }y. \tag{64}
\]
There are finitely many outcome cells.  Hence
\[
 b_\star:=\min_y B_{R_C,y}(P)>0. \tag{65}
\]
Each \(B_{R_C,y}\) is a polynomial by \(\mathrm{def{:}truncated\text{-}functional}\).  Polynomial continuity and (65) therefore give an open neighborhood \(U\) of \(P\) such that
\[
 \min_y B_{R_C,y}(p)>b_\star/2>0
 \qquad(p\in U). \tag{66}
\]
On \(U\), every coordinate of \(\tau_C\) is a quotient of polynomials with a nonzero denominator.  Consequently \(\tau_C\) is infinitely differentiable on \(U\), its derivative is \(J_{\tau_C}\), and \(J_{\tau_C}\) is continuous on \(U\).

Let \(m=|\Omega|\), let \(e_z\in\mathbb R^m\) be the coordinate vector of cell \(z\), and define
\[
 W_i=e_{Z_i}-P. \tag{67}
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}iid\text{-}multinomial}\) and the definition of \(\widehat p_n\) imply
\[
 \mathbb E_PW_i=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_P(W_iW_i^{\mathsf T})
 =\operatorname{diag}(P)-PP^{\mathsf T}=\Sigma_P, \tag{68}
\]
and
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat p_n-P)
 =n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n W_i. \tag{69}
\]
The vectors \(W_i\) have finite support, so \(\mathbb E_P\|W_i\|^2<\infty\).  Applying \(\mathrm{lem{:}multivariate\text{-}iid\text{-}clt}\) to (68)--(69) gives
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat p_n-P)\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_P), \tag{70}
\]
where the covariance matrix may be singular.  Directly from independence and (68),
\[
 \mathbb E_P\|\widehat p_n-P\|_2^2
 =\frac{\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma_P)}{n}\longrightarrow0. \tag{71}
\]
Thus \(\widehat p_n\to P\) in probability.  Since \(U\) is an open neighborhood of \(P\), (66)--(71) imply
\[
 \Pr_P\!\left\{\min_yB_{R_C,y}(\widehat p_n)>0\right\}
 \geq \Pr_P(\widehat p_n\in U)\longrightarrow1. \tag{72}
\]
This proves the asserted probability limit for the defining event in \(\mathrm{def{:}plugin\text{-}estimator}\).

Define the everywhere-defined local version
\[
 \widetilde\tau_{C,n}
 =\begin{cases}
   \tau_C(\widehat p_n),&\widehat p_n\in U,\\
   \tau_C(P),&\widehat p_n\notin U.
  \end{cases} \tag{73}
\]
On \(\{\widehat p_n\in U\}\), differentiability gives
\[
 \tau_C(\widehat p_n)-\tau_C(P)
 =J_{\tau_C}(P)(\widehat p_n-P)+r(\widehat p_n-P),
 \qquad
 \frac{\|r(h)\|}{\|h\|}\longrightarrow0. \tag{74}
\]
Equation (70) implies \(\sqrt n\|\widehat p_n-P\|=O_P(1)\), while (71)--(72) ensure that the expansion in (74) applies with probability tending to one.  Thus \(\sqrt n r(\widehat p_n-P)=o_P(1)\).  The multivariate delta method \(\mathrm{lem{:}multivariate\text{-}delta\text{-}method}\), equivalently applied through (70) and (74), yields
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widetilde\tau_{C,n}-\tau_C(P)\}
 \Rightarrow
 \mathcal N\!\left(0,V_C(P)\right),
 \qquad
 V_C(P):=J_{\tau_C}(P)\Sigma_PJ_{\tau_C}(P)^{\mathsf T}. \tag{75}
\]
By definition, \(\widehat\tau_{C,n}=\widetilde\tau_{C,n}\) whenever \(\widehat p_n\in U\).  Changing a random vector on an event whose probability tends to zero does not change its weak limit: indeed, for every bounded continuous \(h\), the absolute difference of the two expectations of \(h\) is at most twice the supremum norm of \(h\) times the probability of that event.  Hence (72) and (75) give
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_{C,n}-\tau_C(P)\}
 \Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,V_C(P)). \tag{76}
\]

The maps
\[
 p\longmapsto\operatorname{diag}(p)-pp^{\mathsf T}
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 p\longmapsto J_{\tau_C}(p) \tag{77}
\]
are continuous at \(P\), the latter by (66).  Equations (71)--(72), continuity of matrix multiplication, and the definition of \(\widehat V_{C,n}\) therefore imply
\[
 \widehat\Sigma_n\xrightarrow{P}\Sigma_P,
 \qquad
 J_{\tau_C}(\widehat p_n)\xrightarrow{P}J_{\tau_C}(P),
 \qquad
 \widehat V_{C,n}\xrightarrow{P}V_C(P). \tag{78}
\]
As in (76), the stipulated off-event value does not affect the probability limit because the complement of the defining event has probability tending to zero.

Fix a contrast \(a\) and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), and suppose
\[
 v_{C,a}:=a^{\mathsf T}V_C(P)a>0. \tag{79}
\]
Applying the delta method to the linear map \(t\mapsto a^{\mathsf T}t\) in (76), and applying (78), gives
\[
 \sqrt n\,a^{\mathsf T}\{\widehat\tau_{C,n}-\tau_C(P)\}
 \Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,v_{C,a}),
 \qquad
 a^{\mathsf T}\widehat V_{C,n}a\xrightarrow{P}v_{C,a}. \tag{80}
\]
The second convergence and (79) also show that \(a^{\mathsf T}\widehat V_{C,n}a>0\) with probability tending to one.  The scalar Slutsky result \(\mathrm{lem{:}slutsky\text{-}scalar}\) applied to (80) yields
\[
 \frac{\sqrt n\,a^{\mathsf T}\{\widehat\tau_{C,n}-\tau_C(P)\}}
 {\sqrt{a^{\mathsf T}\widehat V_{C,n}a}}
 \Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1). \tag{81}
\]
Let \(z_{1-\alpha/2}=\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)\).  The standard normal distribution is continuous at \(\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\), so (81), the definition of the quantile, and symmetry of the standard normal law give
\[
 \Pr_P\!\left[
 \left|
 \frac{\sqrt n\,a^{\mathsf T}\{\widehat\tau_{C,n}-\tau_C(P)\}}
 {\sqrt{a^{\mathsf T}\widehat V_{C,n}a}}
 \right|
 \leq z_{1-\alpha/2}
 \right]
 \longrightarrow
 \Phi(z_{1-\alpha/2})-\Phi(-z_{1-\alpha/2})
 =1-\alpha. \tag{82}
\]
By (63), the center \(a^{\mathsf T}\tau_C(P)\) in (82) equals \(a^{\mathsf T}P_x^D(Y)\) for every fixed \(D\in C\).  Rearranging the event in (82) proves the asserted contrast interval.

For the coordinate contrast \(a=e_y\), (79) becomes
\[
 \sigma_{C,y}^2
 =e_y^{\mathsf T}J_{\tau_C}(P)\Sigma_PJ_{\tau_C}(P)^{\mathsf T}e_y>0, \tag{83}
\]
which is precisely the positive coordinate-variance condition in the theorem.  Replacing the exact quantile in (82) by \(1.96\) gives limiting coverage
\[
 \Pr\{-1.96\leq Z\leq1.96\}
 =2\Phi(1.96)-1
 =0.9500042097\ldots,
 \qquad Z\sim\mathcal N(0,1). \tag{84}
\]
Finally, every application of (70)--(81) treats \(\mathcal I\), the quotient, \(C\), and its circuit as fixed independently of the inference sample.  If any of these objects is selected from \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n\), the estimator can switch rational maps across selection boundaries, and the preceding fixed-map argument supplies no coverage statement.  This proves both the stated scope restriction and all positive assertions.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Theorem 3 (fixed-class plug-in inference).  Fix a finite input \(\mathfrak u\) accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\) for which \(\operatorname{SparseSIM\text{-}ID}\) returns case (iii), fix one returned quotient class \(C\), let \(R_C\) be its canonical representative, and fix \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\).  The exact oracle and the class are treated as population-fixed objects, or as externally certified true objects that are independent of \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n\).  Put
\[
 \tau_C(p)=\bigl(T_{R_C,y}(p)\bigr)_y.
\]
For every \(D\in C\) and every recursive Markovian structural causal model compatible with \(D\) and having observational law \(P\),
\[
 \tau_C(P)=P_x^D(Y).
\]
Every denominator recorded in the representative circuit is positive at \(P\); hence \(\tau_C\) is continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of \(P\), the event defining \(\widehat\tau_{C,n}\) has probability tending to one, and
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_{C,n}-\tau_C(P)\}
 \Rightarrow
 \mathcal N\!\left(0,
 J_{\tau_C}(P)\Sigma_PJ_{\tau_C}(P)^{\mathsf T}\right).
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \widehat V_{C,n}\xrightarrow{P}
 J_{\tau_C}(P)\Sigma_PJ_{\tau_C}(P)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
For any fixed contrast vector \(a\) of matching dimension and any fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), if
\[
 a^{\mathsf T}J_{\tau_C}(P)\Sigma_PJ_{\tau_C}(P)^{\mathsf T}a>0,
\]
then, writing \(\Phi\) for the standard normal distribution function, the Wald interval
\[
 a^{\mathsf T}\widehat\tau_{C,n}
 \ \pm\ 
 \Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)
 \sqrt{\frac{a^{\mathsf T}\widehat V_{C,n}a}{n}}
\]
has limiting coverage \(1-\alpha\) for \(a^{\mathsf T}P_x^D(Y)\), simultaneously in the sense that the same assertion holds for every fixed \(D\in C\).  In particular, if \(\sigma_{C,y}^2>0\), then
\[
 \widehat\tau_{C,n,y}\pm1.96\sqrt{\widehat V_{C,n,yy}/n}
\]
has limiting coverage \(2\Phi(1.96)-1=0.9500042097\ldots\) for \(P_x^D(Y=y)\), for every fixed \(D\in C\).  These conclusions do not cover data-driven selection of the oracle or quotient class from \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n\) without an additional selection-inference argument.

The replacement narrows the coverage guarantee to a population-fixed or externally certified true class independent of the inference sample, while carrying the same proved fixed-circuit argument to every returned class and exposing its fixed-contrast Wald consequence as required by the active directive.

proposed.justification: A certified classwise population functional should yield one standard sampling analysis without graphwise duplicate estimates.
proposed.gap: Chang, Guo, and Malinsky handle data-driven graph selection by interval unions; this theorem gives pointwise plug-in inference only after the exact oracle and a true returned quotient class are fixed or externally certified independently of the inference sample.
proposed.consumer: After a population or external certification analysis, practitioners can estimate any fixed contrast of the intervention law common to a returned quotient class with one covariance calculation.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The theorem is synchronized with the class-indexed estimator and states the fixed-class causal equality, multivariate limit, sandwich consistency, arbitrary fixed-contrast Wald interval, numerical coordinate corollary, and selection scope required by the active directive.
